item.title: Fresh narratives on Management Development
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores innovative approaches to management development in response to contemporary challenges including geopolitical instability, technological disruption, and sustainability pressures. It seeks concise research reports that examine how managers can be trained and equipped to navigate rapidly changing business environments and respond effectively to emerging complexities that traditional management studies only partially address.

The special issue welcomes empirical research using various methodologies that advance management development theory and practice. It particularly encourages contributions from early career researchers that offer fresh perspectives on redesigning management training for both individual and organisational levels, emphasizing practical applications and interdisciplinary insights on topics such as AI integration, nearshoring, and sustainable digital transformation.

Appel publié par Journal of Management Development. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developing managerial competencies for leading sustainable digital transformation
  • Responsible AI integration into management development programmes, including leadership training, upskilling and CPD
  • Cross-cultural management development for geographically integrated teams and supply chains, including nearshoring and regional hubs
  • Management development for inclusive and responsible entrepreneurial ecosystems, embedding DEI, well-being and AI-enabled work transformation into entrepreneurial training
  • The critical role of human agency in managing robotic and AI integration, including developing managerial frameworks for responsible AI governance as autonomous systems outpace ethical and regulatory preparedness

Timeline

  • January 12, 2026: Closing date for abstract submission
  • September 30, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • March 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Developing Management Capability in Sustainability Leadership
item.content:encoded:
Scott Lichtenstein, Birmingham City University Business School

Paul Aitken, Nelson-Marlborough Institute of Technology

Krish Saha, Birmingham City University Business School

Helen Kopnina, University of Northumbria

Truzaar Dordi, University of York

This special issue seeks interdisciplinary research exploring how managers can develop sustainability leadership capacity across interconnected levels. The focus spans macro outcomes related to compassionate flourishing and planetary health, meso-level organizational and community goals, and micro-level personal values and behavioral inputs of managers. The issue aims to identify connection points in the entire sustainability leadership development system.

Through contributions from diverse scholars, the special issue will examine how sustainability leadership capability can serve as a positive force in addressing global challenges, how it can be applied systematically within organizations and communities, and how managers' personal values and morals translate into sustainable behaviors and decisions. Recommendations emerging from the issue are intended to benefit academics, practitioners, and broader environmental outcomes.

Appel publié par Journal of Management Development. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Sustainability leadership capability development for managers as a force for positive change and compassionate flourishing
  • Anthropocentric assumptions limiting leaders' engagement with planetary health and multi-species justice
  • Systematic and systemic application of sustainability leadership capability development for resolving complex and disruptive challenges
  • Personal values and morals as drivers of managers' sustainability leadership behaviors, decisions and actions
  • Benevolent influence through individual and collective agency in sustainability leadership development

Timeline

  • January 9, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • December 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions
